title: Orders CSV export breaks on customer names with commas or quotes
description:
Several customers report that the orders CSV export opens with shifted columns in Excel. Root cause found by support: names like `Smith, John` and company names like `Acme "Rocket" Ltd` are written unescaped. Examples from real exports:

    1042,Smith, John,2026-03-02,149.00
    1043,Acme "Rocket" Ltd,2026-03-03,2210.50

The export must produce RFC 4180 compliant CSV: fields containing a comma, a double quote or a newline are wrapped in double quotes, and any double quote inside a quoted field is doubled. The header row and column order must not change.
environment: Python 3.12. Service: exports. Used by the dashboard Download button and by the scheduled S3 export.
comments: backend-dev: We build rows by hand with join(). I would rather not pull in the csv module just for this, the helper is tiny.
support-lead: Please also make sure newlines in the notes column are handled, one customer has multi-line notes.
diff:
diff --git a/exports/orders_csv.py b/exports/orders_csv.py
--- a/exports/orders_csv.py
+++ b/exports/orders_csv.py
@@ -1,18 +1,28 @@
 from typing import Iterable

 HEADER = ["order_id", "customer", "created", "total"]

+
+def _escape(value: object) -> str:
+    text = str(value)
+    if "," in text or "\n" in text or '"' in text:
+        return '"' + text + '"'
+    return text
+

 def render(rows: Iterable[dict]) -> str:
     lines = [",".join(HEADER)]
     for row in rows:
         lines.append(
             ",".join(
-                str(row[col]) for col in HEADER
+                _escape(row[col]) for col in HEADER
             )
         )
     return "\r\n".join(lines) + "\r\n"
